headline: Senate Pushes Residential Gun-Storage Checks and Tougher Penalties After Zamboanga Shooting
seoTitle: Senate Pushes Mandatory Gun Safe Checks | FMB News
seoDescription: Senate proposals seek stricter firearm-storage verification and stronger penalties for unsecured guns following the fatal Zamboanga school shooting.
deck: Lawmakers are proposing tighter verification of home firearm storage and stronger liability when unsecured weapons are accessed by minors or other unauthorized persons.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Senate lawmakers are pushing amendments to Republic Act No. 10591 that would tighten firearm-storage requirements following the fatal Zamboanga school shooting, according to the approved FMB News evening brief.

The package says Senator Raffy Tulfo and other lawmakers are proposing stronger verification of residential firearm storage before licenses are issued or renewed, along with tougher penalties when unsecured guns are accessed by minors or other unauthorized individuals.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Republic Act No. 10591 already requires licensed firearm owners to keep firearms in a vault, a container secured by lock and key, or through other security measures. The law also imposes additional inspection and bond requirements on some higher-tier license categories.

The new proposals described in the newsroom brief would go further by making storage verification more explicit and by increasing owner accountability when negligent safekeeping contributes to unauthorized access.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The policy question is no longer only who may legally own a firearm. It is also how licensed owners are expected to store weapons in homes and vehicles, and what consequences should follow when those safeguards fail.
Because the measures remain legislative proposals, their final scope, inspection mechanism and penalties may change during committee deliberations.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the filed bill text, committee referral, hearing schedule and any PNP Firearms and Explosives Office position on how storage inspections could be implemented without creating inconsistent or intrusive enforcement practices.
